US April close items are done. Summary of what I posted:

**JE-00307 — Depreciation, $3,425** (Dr 6800 / Cr 1510). Per the April fixed asset register (DOC-0208): $164,400 of computer equipment, straight-line over 36 months, no April additions or disposals. Verified 6800 YTD is now $13,700 = 4 × $3,425.

**JE-00308 — Prepaid software amortization, $1,250** (Dr 6200 / Cr 1210). Figtree annual license, $15,000 over 12 months (DOC-0209/DOC-0068). Verified 1210 now sits at $10,000 = 8 remaining months.

**JE-00309 — Parker & Rowe invoice PR-4410, $17,350** (Dr 2100 $14,250, Dr 6500 $3,100, Cr 2000 $17,350).

The key judgment: the invoice bundles two service periods. The $14,250 Series B side-letter work is **March** service already expensed via the March accrual JE-00306 — the invoice matched the vendor's estimate exactly, so I relieved the accrual in full against 2100 with no P&L true-up. Only the $3,100 April board materials review hits April expense. Confirmed: 6500 April activity = $3,100, YTD $17,350 with no double count.

Two things needing your attention:

1. **JE-00309 is pending your approval** — $17,350 exceeds my $10,000 limit. I kept it as a single entry rather than splitting the accrual relief from the April expense, since the policy prohibits splitting to stay under the threshold.

2. **Exception EXC-001** — JE-00306, the March accrual, is *still* in pending_approval status despite March being closed. April's entry depends on it, so if that accrual gets rejected or revised, JE-00309 has to move with it. Worth actioning both together.

I left **AP cutoff review open** — I only handled the one invoice you flagged, not a full April cutoff sweep, so it would be misleading to mark it complete.
